capitals.note: Infobox: 'Sandy Bay' with 'Bluefields (after 1787)'; the Reserve's own capital is not named for 1860-1894 (the page mentions only 'the territory around Bluefields').

rulers.name: George Augustus Frederic II
rulers.title: King; hereditary chief after the constitution of 13 September 1861
rulers.note: The page's list gives 1841–1865; the infobox gives him as last ruler of the kingdom 1842–1860 and first ruler of the Reserve 1860–1865. The constitution of 13 September 1861 confirmed him 'only as hereditary chief and not king'. His reign began before this dossier's 1844 start. The span is clipped to the dossier's 1844 start (reviewer am-08-g); the page's list has 1841.

region.text: the coast from Cabo Gracias a Dios to the San Juan River, without the Honduran cells

ledger.note: 1844: Britain declares a new protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom. 'In 1844, the British government declared a new protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom', claimed to run 'from Cape Honduras in the north to the mouth of the San Juan River in the south'. The kingdom itself is older (infobox 'Early 17th century'; a king visited England 'around 1638' and sealed an alliance, a Treaty of Friendship and Alliance followed in 1740); this is the first year the dossier draws it, on the Cliopatria outline.

ledger.note: 1846: the eastern Honduran Mosquitia joins the Kingdom's outline. Cliopatria moves the 21 cells of Gracias a Dios out of Honduras in 1846; the page is silent on a cession, giving only the 1844 protectorate over the coast 'from Cape Honduras'.

region.text: San Juan del Norte (Greytown) at the mouth of the San Juan River

ledger.note: 1848: Britain and the Miskito seize San Juan del Norte. After the ultimatum expired, 'Miskito-British forces led by the King and Patrick Walker, and backed by two British warships, seized San Juan del Norte' (the sentence is undated; the year comes from the ultimatum 'before 1 January 1848' and 'the 1848 peace treaty'; reviewer am-08-g corrected the quote).

region.text: San Juan del Norte (Greytown) at the mouth of the San Juan River

ledger.note: 7 March 1848: Nicaragua cedes San Juan del Norte. 'On 7 March Nicaragua signed a peace treaty where it ceded San Juan del Norte to the Mosquito Kingdom'; the town was renamed Greytown. The Nicaragua dossier puts the town at about 759 km2, below the grid's resolution of change, so the shapes do not show it.

ledger.note: 1859: Britain cedes the northern Mosquito Coast to Honduras. 'The British government returned the Bay Islands and ceded the northern part of the Mosquito Coast to Honduras'; the page gives no treaty or day, and 'the northern part' is read as the Honduran cells north of Cabo Gracias a Dios.

28 January 1860: the Treaty of Managua turns the Kingdom into the Mosquito Reserve. 'Britain and Nicaragua signed the Treaty of Managua on 28 January 1860', transferring 'suzerainty over the Caribbean coast between Cabo Gracias a Dios and Greytown to Nicaragua'; the Kingdom 'would become an autonomous Miskito reserve'. The ruler became 'hereditary chief and not king' by the municipal constitution of 13 September 1861. The relation is Nicaragua's vassal event, counterpart this slug; no land changes hands.

ledger.note: 20 November 1894: Nicaragua incorporates the Mosquito Reserve. 'On 20 November 1894 their territory formally became incorporated into that of the republic of Nicaragua' under José Santos Zelaya, as the department of Zelaya.

ledger.note: 20 November 1894: the Mosquito Reserve ends. The Reserve's territory is incorporated into Nicaragua (infobox end event 'Annexation to Nicaragua').

wars.name: Miskito–British seizure of San Juan del Norte

zones.text: San Juan del Norte (Greytown) at the mouth of the San Juan River

wars.outcome: Britain and the Miskito seize San Juan del Norte in 1848 and on 7 March Nicaragua signs a peace treaty ceding it to the Mosquito Kingdom, which renames it Greytown.
wars.note: The Clayton-Bulwer Treaty (18 April 1850) between the United States and Britain forbade either power to 'occupy, or fortify, or colonize, or assume or exercise any dominion over Nicaragua'; it moved no border on the page. Britain occupied the Bay Islands in 1852 and returned them in 1859 (Honduras dossier).

certainty.note: The protectorate's claimed limits (Cape Honduras to the San Juan) were larger than any drawn line; the inland edge was never fixed.

The Treaty of Managua fixes the coast 'between Cabo Gracias a Dios and Greytown' but gives no inland line; the northern boundary along the Coco (Wanks) River was disputed from 1869 (Nicaragua dossier).

notes: Cliopatria's row is 1853-1859 only (two shapes, the same 26,801 km2 outline). The Mosquito Kingdom is older (infobox 'Early 17th century'; king's visit to England 'around 1638'); the page dates no founding year and gives no territory before the 1844 protectorate, so this dossier starts in 1844 (a drawing choice, not the founding) and the earlier centuries are left to a gap-filler. The dossier runs on as the Mosquito Reserve to 20 November 1894, as the Nicaragua dossier asks (its vassal_start of 1860-01 and vassal_end/gain of 1894-11 name this slug): from 1860 the strip is drawn through those vassal events; this dossier supplies the identity and the keyframe, and the renderer should draw the strip once. The Honduras dossier loses 21 cells to this slug in 1846 and regains them in 1859, as the ledger mirrors; the pages give neither event a day. Page conflicts: the page's king list gives George Augustus Frederic II 1841-1865 while its infobox has him as last king 1842-1860 and first chief 1860-1865; the lead says the Reserve stayed autonomous to 1894 while the section 'now reduced to the territory around Bluefields' suggests a smaller core after 1860 (not drawn).
